What mathematical concept, originating in India, was transmitted to the Arab world and later to Europe, revolutionizing calculation methods?
A) Geometry  
B) Zero and the decimal system  
C) Algebraic symbols  
D) Calculus

What mathematical concept, originating in India, was transmitted to the Arab world and later to Europe, revolutionizing calculation methods?
A) Geometry  
B) Zero and the decimal system  
C) Algebraic symbols  
D) Calculus
questions.a:
B) Zero and the decimal system.  
If a student chooses A) Geometry, they confuse Indian contributions with Greek strengths, missing that while Indians used geometry, their unique global impact was the place-value system and zero. Choosing D) Calculus shows a chronological error—calculus developed much later in Europe.

A 9th-century Persian physician’s manual includes descriptions of surgical instruments and herbal remedies identical to those in Sushruta Samhita. How would you explain this similarity?
A) The Persian physician copied directly from Sushruta without credit  
B) Independent invention of surgery in both regions  
C) Knowledge transfer via scholars at the Abbasid Caliphate’s Baghdad House of Wisdom  
D) The Persian text is a forgery made to claim Indian knowledge

A 9th-century Persian physician’s manual includes descriptions of surgical instruments and herbal remedies identical to those in Sushruta Samhita. How would you explain this similarity?
A) The Persian physician copied directly from Sushruta without credit  
B) Independent invention of surgery in both regions  
C) Knowledge transfer via scholars at the Abbasid Caliphate’s Baghdad House of Wisdom  
D) The Persian text is a forgery made to claim Indian knowledge
questions.a:
C) Knowledge transfer via scholars at the Abbasid Caliphate’s Baghdad House of Wisdom.  
If a student picks A), they miss the institutional context of exchange—scholars were invited to translate and share knowledge, not steal it. Choosing B) ignores the low probability of identical complex surgical tools arising independently. Selecting D) reflects a conspiracy mindset unsupported by manuscript evidence showing clear translation trails.

Compare the direction of knowledge flow in astronomy between India and Greece during 500 BCE–500 CE. Which statement is most accurate?
A) India only received Greek astronomical knowledge; gave nothing in return  
B) Greece only received Indian astronomical knowledge; gave nothing in return  
C) Mutual exchange occurred: Indians adopted Greek geometric models, Greeks adopted Indian planetary calculations  
D) No significant exchange happened; both developed astronomy in isolation

Compare the direction of knowledge flow in astronomy between India and Greece during 500 BCE–500 CE. Which statement is most accurate?
A) India only received Greek astronomical knowledge; gave nothing in return  
B) Greece only received Indian astronomical knowledge; gave nothing in return  
C) Mutual exchange occurred: Indians adopted Greek geometric models, Greeks adopted Indian planetary calculations  
D) No significant exchange happened; both developed astronomy in isolation
questions.a:
C) Mutual exchange occurred: Indians adopted Greek geometric models, Greeks adopted Indian planetary calculations.  
Choosing A) or B) reflects a one-way transfer myth—ignoring that Indians used Greek epicycles while Greeks like Ptolemy referenced Indian sine tables. Picking D) contradicts evidence of Indo-Greek schools and translated texts showing bidirectional influence.

questions.q:
Evaluate the claim: “The spread of Ayurveda to Southeast Asia was primarily due to Indian merchants, not scholars or monks.” Is this claim justified? Defend your position with evidence.
A) Yes, because merchants carried goods and could easily share medical knowledge  
B) No, because Ayurveda’s complexity required scholarly transmission via monastic networks  
C) Partly yes—merchants introduced basics, but monks adapted it locally  
D) No, because Southeast Asia developed its own medicine independently

Evaluate the claim: “The spread of Ayurveda to Southeast Asia was primarily due to Indian merchants, not scholars or monks.” Is this claim justified? Defend your position with evidence.
A) Yes, because merchants carried goods and could easily share medical knowledge  
B) No, because Ayurvedic complexity required scholarly transmission via monastic networks  
C) Partly yes—merchants introduced basics, but monks adapted it locally  
D) No, because Southeast Asia developed its own medicine independently
questions.a:
C) Partly yes—merchants introduced basics, but monks adapted it locally.  
Choosing A) oversimplifies—merchants might share remedies, but complex diagnostics need training. Selecting B) ignores merchant roles in spreading rudimentary knowledge. Picking D) denies clear linguistic and textual evidence of Indian origin in Javanese and Balinese Ayurvedic texts. The best answer acknowledges layered transmission: merchants opened the door, monastic scholars deepened and localized it.

questions.q:
Create a timeline showing three key moments of knowledge exchange in medicine between India and the Arab world from 700–1100 CE, labeling each with the agent of transfer and the knowledge shared.
A) 750 CE: Arab traders bring Indian textiles to Basra; share weaving techniques  
B) 800 CE: Scholars at Baghdad’s House of Wisdom translate Sushruta Samhita into Arabic; share surgical knowledge  
C) 850 CE: Indian monks spread Ayurveda via maritime trade to Malacca; share herbal remedies  
D) 1000 CE: Persian doctors visit Nalanda; learn vaccination techniques

Create a timeline showing three key moments of knowledge exchange in medicine between India and the Arab world from 700–1100 CE, labeling each with the agent of transfer and the knowledge shared.
A) 750 CE: Arab traders bring Indian textiles to Basra; share weaving techniques  
B) 800 CE: Scholars at Baghdad’s House of Wisdom translate Sushruta Samhita into Arabic; share surgical knowledge  
C) 850 CE: Indian monks spread Ayurveda via maritime trade to Malacca; share herbal remedies  
D) 1000 CE: Persian doctors visit Nalanda; learn vaccination techniques
questions.a:
B) 800 CE: Scholars at Baghdad’s House of Wisdom translate Sushruta Samhita into Arabic; share surgical knowledge is correct.  
A) confuses medicine with textiles. C) misplaces location (Malacca is Southeast Asia, not Arab world) and overstates monk roles in medicine transfer. D) is anachronistic—vaccination wasn’t known until 18th century. A strong answer would note: 770 CE (Charaka Samhita translated at Baghdad), 850 CE (Arab physicians use Indian pulse diagnosis in Cairo), 1025 CE (Al-Biruni’s India cites Ayurvedic pharmacology).
